questions.q: What does the `region` attribute in a `provider "aws"` block control?
options: Which IAM user Terraform authenticates as
Which AWS region resources are created in, unless a resource overrides it
Which version of the AWS CLI is installed
Which Terraform workspace is active
questions.explain: The region attribute tells every aws_* resource in the configuration which AWS region to provision into by default.

questions.q: Which of these is a safe way to authenticate the `aws` provider?
options: Hardcoding `access_key` and `secret_key` directly in the provider block
Pasting access keys into a comment above the provider block
Referencing a named AWS CLI profile stored in `~/.aws/credentials`
Committing a `.aws` folder to the same Git repo as the Terraform code
questions.explain: A named CLI profile keeps credentials out of the .tf files entirely, pointing Terraform at credentials already stored locally by the AWS CLI.

questions.q: Why are environment variables like `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` a common authentication choice in CI pipelines?
options: They are the only authentication method Terraform supports
CI runners often have no persistent home directory to store a CLI profile in
They are automatically encrypted by Terraform
They replace the need for a provider block entirely
questions.explain: CI pipelines frequently run in ephemeral environments with no lasting ~/.aws/credentials file, so environment variables the provider reads automatically are the practical alternative.

questions.q: What is the main risk of hardcoding an AWS access key inside a `.tf` file?
options: Terraform will refuse to run the configuration
The key becomes a permanent leak the moment it's committed to version control
It will slow down `terraform plan`
It only affects the `terraform fmt` command
questions.explain: Once a secret is committed to version control, it's effectively exposed permanently — even deleting it later doesn't remove it from history.

questions.q: What does `terraform init` do the first time it runs against the `aws` provider?
options: It creates the AWS account automatically
It downloads the provider plugin matching the version constraint and records it in a lockfile
It provisions the first EC2 instance
It deletes any existing AWS resources before starting fresh
questions.explain: terraform init downloads the provider plugin version that satisfies the required_providers constraint and locks it in .terraform.lock.hcl, before any plan or apply can run.
